| [New resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md")                                                                                                                             | The following resources were added: `AWS::Cases::Domain`, `AWS::Cases::Field`, `AWS::Cases::Layout`, `AWS::Cases::CaseRule`, and `AWS::Cases::Template`.<br>[AWS::Cases::Domain](../UserGuide/aws-resource-cases-domain.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-cases-domain.md")<br>Use the `AWS::Cases::Domain` resource to create a domain, which is a container for all case data, such as cases, fields, templates and layouts. Each Amazon Connect instance can be associated with only one Cases domain.<br>[AWS::Cases::Field](../UserGuide/aws-resource-cases-field.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-cases-field.md")<br>Use the `AWS::Cases::Field` resource to create a field in the Cases domain. This field is used to define the case object model (that is, defines what data can be captured on cases) in a Cases domain.<br>[AWS::Cases::Layout](../UserGuide/aws-resource-cases-layout.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-cases-layout.md")<br>Use the `AWS::Cases::Layout` resource to create a layout in the Cases domain. Layouts define the following configuration in the top section and More Info tab of the Cases user interface: Fields to display to the users and Field ordering.<br>[AWS::Cases::CaseRule](../UserGuide/aws-resource-cases-caserule.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-cases-caserule.md")<br>Use the `AWS::Cases::CaseRule` resource to create a case rule. In the Amazon Connect admin website, case rules are known as case field conditions. Case rules are used to define the situations under which fields should have certain effects (such as required).<br>[AWS::Cases::Template](../UserGuide/aws-resource-cases-template.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-cases-template.md")<br>Use the `AWS::Cases::Template` resource to create a template in the Cases domain. This template is used to define the case object model (that is, to define what data can be captured on cases) in a Cases domain. A template must have a unique name within a domain, and it must reference existing field IDs and layout IDs.             | The following resources were updated with enhanced semantic versioning, logging, and pipeline management features: AWS::ImageBuilder::Component, AWS::ImageBuilder::ContainerRecipe, AWS::ImageBuilder::Image, AWS::ImageBuilder::ImagePipeline, AWS::ImageBuilder::ImageRecipe, and AWS::ImageBuilder::Workflow.<br>[AWS::ImageBuilder::Component](../UserGuide/aws-resource-imagebuilder-component.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-imagebuilder-component.md"),<br>[AWS::ImageBuilder::ContainerRecipe](../UserGuide/aws-resource-imagebuilder-containerrecipe.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-imagebuilder-containerrecipe.md"),<br>[AWS::ImageBuilder::ImageRecipe](../UserGuide/aws-resource-imagebuilder-imagerecipe.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-imagebuilder-imagerecipe.md"),<br>[AWS::ImageBuilder::Workflow](../UserGuide/aws-resource-imagebuilder-workflow.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-imagebuilder-workflow.md")<br>• Enhanced semantic versioning support with detailed documentation for version assignment and patterns.<br>• Added `LatestVersion` return values with wildcard variations for semantic versioning, including `Arn`, `Major`, `Minor`, and `Patch` properties.<br>[AWS::ImageBuilder::ImageRecipe](../UserGuide/aws-resource-imagebuilder-imagerecipe.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-imagebuilder-imagerecipe.md")<br>Added `AmiTags` property to apply tags to AMIs created during the Build phase prior to image distribution.<br>[AWS::ImageBuilder::Image](../UserGuide/aws-resource-imagebuilder-image.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-imagebuilder-image.md")<br>• Added `LoggingConfiguration` property to define custom log group names for image creation.<br>• Added `DeletionSettings` for automatic cleanup of underlying resources when images are replaced or deleted.<br>• Introduced `ImagePipelineExecutionSettings` with deployment ID support and configurable execution triggers on pipeline updates.<br>[AWS::ImageBuilder::ImagePipeline](../UserGuide/aws-resource-imagebuilder-imagepipeline.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-imagebuilder-imagepipeline.md")<br>• Added `LoggingConfiguration` property to define custom log group names for pipeline execution.<br>• Enhanced pipeline management with `AutoDisablePolicy` to automatically disable failing pipelines after a specified number of consecutive failures. | [Updated resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md")                                                                                                                         | The following resources were updated: `AWS::CleanRooms::AnalysisTemplate`, `AWS::CleanRooms::Collaboration`, `AWS::CleanRooms::Membership`, and `AWS::CleanRooms::ConfiguredTable`.<br>[AWS::CleanRooms::AnalysisTemplate](../UserGuide/aws-resource-cleanrooms-analysistemplate.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-cleanrooms-analysistemplate.md")<br>Use the `AnalysisTemplateArtifacts` property to specify the entry point and additional artifacts for the analysis template.<br>Use the `SourceMetadata` property to specify the source metadata for the analysis template.<br>Use the `Schema` property to specify the entire schema object for the analysis template.<br>In the [Hash](../UserGuide/aws-properties-cleanrooms-analysistemplate-hash.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-cleanrooms-analysistemplate-hash.md") property type, use the `Sha256` property to specify the SHA-256 hash value.<br>In the [S3Location](../UserGuide/aws-properties-cleanrooms-analysistemplate-s3location.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-cleanrooms-analysistemplate-s3location.md") property type, use the `Bucket` property to specify the bucket name and the `Key` property to specify the object key.<br>mw<br>[AWS::CleanRooms::Collaboration](../UserGuide/aws-resource-cleanrooms-collaboration.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-cleanrooms-collaboration.md")<br>Use the `JobComputePaymentConfig` property to specify payment responsibilities for query and job compute costs.<br>Use the `PaymentConfiguration` property to specify the<br>compute configuration for the job.<br>Use the `JobLogStatus` property to enable or disable job logging for the collaboration.<br>In the [ProtectedJobS3OutputConfigurationInput](../UserGuide/aws-properties-cleanrooms-membership-protectedjobs3outputconfigurationinput.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-cleanrooms-membership-protectedjobs3outputconfigurationinput.md") property type, use the `Bucket` property to specify the S3 bucket for job output and the `KeyPrefix` property to specify the S3 prefix to unload the protected job results.<br>[AWS::CleanRooms::Membership](../UserGuide/aws-resource-cleanrooms-membership.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-cleanrooms-membership.md")<br>Use the `MembershipProtectedJobResultConfiguration` property to specify configurations for protected job results.<br>Use the `MembershipJobComputePaymentConfig` property to specify the payment responsibilities for job compute costs.<br>Use the `DefaultJobResultConfiguration` property to specify the default job result configuration for the membership.<br>Use the `JobLogStatus` property to enable or disable job logging for the membership.<br>[AWS::CleanRooms::ConfiguredTable](../UserGuide/aws-resource-cleanrooms-configuredtable.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-cleanrooms-configuredtable.md")<br>Use the `SelectedAnalysisMethods` property to specify the selected analysis methods for the configured table. | [New resource](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md")                                                                                                                              | The following resources were added: `AWS::DataZone::DataSource`,<br>`AWS::DataZone::Domain`, `AWS::DataZone::Environment`,<br>`AWS::DataZone::EnvironmentBlueprintConfiguration`,<br>`AWS::DataZone::EnvironmentProfile`,<br>`AWS::DataZone::Project`,<br>`AWS::DataZone::SubscriptionTarget`.<br>[AWS::DataZone::DataSource](../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-datasource.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-datasource.md")<br>Use the `AWS::DataZone::DataSource` resource to specify<br>an Amazon DataZone data source that is used to import technical<br>metadata of assets (data) from the source databases or data<br>warehouses into Amazon DataZone.<br>[AWS::DataZone::Domain](../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-domain.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-domain.md")<br>Use the `AWS::DataZone::Domain` resource to specify an<br>Amazon DataZone domain. You can use domains to organize your assets,<br>users, and their projects.<br>[AWS::DataZone::Environment](../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-environment.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-environment.md")<br>Use the `AWS::DataZone::Environment` resource to<br>specify an Amazon DataZone environment, which is a collection of<br>zero or more configured resources with a given set of IAM principals<br>who can operate on those resources.<br>[AWS::DataZone::EnvironmentBlueprintConfiguration](../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-environmentblueprintconfiguration.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-environmentblueprintconfiguration.md")<br>Use the<br>`AWS::DataZone::EnvironmentBlueprintConfiguration`<br>resource to specify the configuration details of an environment<br>blueprint.<br>[AWS::DataZone::EnvironmentProfile](../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-environmentprofile.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-environmentprofile.md")<br>Use the `AWS::DataZone::EnvironmentProfile` resource to<br>specify the details of an environment profile.<br>[AWS::DataZone::Project](../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-project.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-project.md")<br>Use the `AWS::DataZone::Project` resource to specify an<br>Amazon DataZone project. Projects enable a group of users to<br>collaborate on various business use cases that involve publishing,<br>discovering, subscribing to, and consuming data in the Amazon<br>DataZone catalog. Project members consume assets from the Amazon<br>DataZone catalog and produce new assets using one or more analytical<br>workflows.<br>[AWS::DataZone::SubscriptionTarget](../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-subscriptiontarget.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-subscriptiontarget.md")<br>Use the `AWS::DataZone::SubscriptionTarget` resource to<br>specify an Amazon DataZone subscription target. Subscription targets<br>enable you to access the data to which you have subscribed in your<br>projects. A subscription target specifies the location (for example,<br>a database or a schema) and the required permissions (for example,<br>an IAM role) that Amazon DataZone can use to establish a connection<br>with the source data and to create the necessary grants so that<br>members of the Amazon DataZone project can start querying the data<br>to which they have subscribed.             | The following resource was added: AWS::RDS::CustomDBEngineVersion<br>[AWS::RDS::CustomDBEngineVersion](../UserGuide/aws-resource-rds-customdbengineversion.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-rds-customdbengineversion.md")<br>The `DatabaseInstallationFilesS3BucketName` property is the name of an<br>Amazon S3 bucket that contains database installation files for your CEV.<br>The `DatabaseInstallationFilesS3Prefix` property is the Amazon S3<br>directory that contains the database installation files for your CEV.<br>Use the `Description` property to provide an optional description of your CEV.<br>Use the `Engine` property to indicate the database engine to use for your custom engine version (CEV).<br>Use the `EngineVersion` property to indicate the name of your CEV in the format `19.customized_string`.<br>Use the `KMSKeyId` property for the AWS KMS key identifier for an encrypted CEV.<br>The `Manifest` property is the CEV manifest, which is a JSON document that describes the installation .zip files stored in Amazon S3.<br>The `Status` property provides the status of a custom engine version (CEV).<br>The `Tags` property allows you to add metadata to your RDS resource. configure how Amazon Lex handles intents.<br>Use the [IntentClosingSetting](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-intentclosingsetting.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-intentclosingsetting.md") property to configure the statement that Amazon Lex<br>conveys to the user when the intent is successfully fulfilled.<br>Use the [IntentConfirmationSetting](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-intentconfirmationsetting.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-intentconfirmationsetting.md") property to provide a prompt for making sure that the user<br>is ready for the intent to be fulfilled.<br>Use the [IntentOverride](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-intentoverride.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-intentoverride.md") property to override settings to configure the intent state.<br>Use the [PostDialogCodeHookInvocationSpecification](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-postdialogcodehookinvocationspecification.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-postdialogcodehookinvocationspecification.md") property<br>to specify next steps to run after the dialog code hook finishes.<br>Use the [PostFulfillmentStatusSpecification](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-postfulfillmentstatusspecification.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-postfulfillmentstatusspecification.md") property to configure the settings of the<br>post-fulfillment response that is sent to the user.<br>Use the [PromptAttemptSpecification](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-promptattemptspecification.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-promptattemptspecification.md") property to specify the settings on a prompt attempt.<br>Use the [PromptSpecification](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-promptspecification.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-promptspecification.md") property to specify a list of message groups that<br>Amazon Lex sends to a user to elicit a response.<br>Use the [SessionAttribute](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-sessionattribute.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-sessionattribute.md") property to specify session-specific context information.<br>Use the [SlotCaptureSetting](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-slotcapturesetting.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-slotcapturesetting.md") property to configure the settings that are used when<br>Amazon Lex successfully captures a slot value from a user.<br>Use the [SlotValue](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-slotvalue.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-slotvalue.md") property to set values in a slot.<br>Use the [SlotValueElicitationSetting](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-slotvalueelicitationsetting.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-slotvalueelicitationsetting.md") property to specify the settings for eliciting a slot value.<br>Use the [SlotValueOverride](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-slotvalueoverride.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-slotvalueoverride.md") property to set slot values in a dialog step.<br>Use the [SlotValueOverrideMap](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-slotvalueoverridemap.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-slotvalueoverridemap.md") property to map slot names to a SlotValueOVerride object.<br>Use the [TextInputSpecification](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-textinputspecification.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-textinputspecification.md") property to specify the text input specifications.<br>Use the [VoiceSettings](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-voicesettings.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-voicesettings.md") property to specify the Amazon Polly voice used for<br>audio interaction with the user. "../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-endpoint.md")<br>Use the `DeploymentConfig` property to specify the deployment<br>configuration for an endpoint, which contains the desired deployment<br>strategy and rollback configurations.<br>Use the `AutoRollbackConfig` property to specify the the<br>automatic rollback configuration for handling endpoint deployment failures<br>and recovery.<br>Use the `Alarm` property to specify a list of CloudWatch<br>alarms that are configured to monitor metrics on an endpoint.<br>Use the `AlarmName` property to specify the name of a<br>CloudWatch alarm in your account.<br>Use the `BlueGreenUpdatePolicy` property to specify the update<br>policy for a blue/green deployment.<br>Use the `MaximumExecutionTimeoutInSeconds` property to specify<br>the maximum execution timeout for a blue/green deployment.<br>Use the `TerminationWaitInSeconds` property to specify<br>additional waiting time in seconds after the completion of an endpoint<br>deployment before terminating the old endpoint fleet<br>Use the `TrafficRoutingConfig` property to specify the traffic<br>routing strategy during a blue/green endpoint deployment.<br>Use the `CanarySize` property to specify the batch size for<br>the first step to turn on traffic on the new endpoint fleet.<br>Use the `LinearStepSize` property to specify the batch size<br>for each step to turn on traffic on the new endpoint fleet<br>Use the `Type` property to specify the traffic routing<br>strategy type (all at once, canary, or linear).<br>Use the `WaitIntervalInSeconds` property to specify the<br>waiting time (in seconds) between incremental steps to turn on traffic on<br>the new endpoint fleet.<br>Use the `CapacitySize` property to specify the endpoint<br>capacity to activate for production.<br>Use the `Type` property to specify the endpoint capacity type<br>to use (instance count or capacity percent).<br>Use the `Value` property to specify the capacity size, either<br>as a number of instances or a capacity percentage.<br>Use the `RetainDeploymentConfig` property to specify whether<br>to reuse the last deployment configuration. The default value is false (the<br>configuration is not reused) transaction.<br>[AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::RoutingControl](../UserGuide/aws-resource-route53recoverycontrol-routingcontrol.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-route53recoverycontrol-routingcontrol.md")<br>Use the `AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::RoutingControl` to fail over traffic to an application replica, to recover your "../UserGuide/aws-resource-route53recoverycontrol-safetyrule.md")<br>Use the `AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::SafetyRule` to configure safeguards for routing controls, to avoid a scenario like<br>stopping all traffic flow by setting all routing controls to off. If you don't specify a value, then AWS Elemental MediaPackage creates the constant initialization vector (IV).<br>[AWS::MediaPackage::PackagingConfiguration.](../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediapackage-packagingconfiguration.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediapackage-packagingconfiguration.md")<br>Use the `CmafPackage.IncludeEncoderConfigurationInSegments` property to place your encoder's metadata into every video segment instead of the init fragment, which is the default behavior. stored in the AWS Glue Data Catalog is defined in<br>a DataBrew dataset.<br>Use the `DatasetParameter` property to define the type<br>and conditions for a parameter in the Amazon S3 path of<br>the dataset.<br>Use the `DatetimeOptions` property to define the<br>correct interpretation of datetime parameters used in the Amazon S3 path of a dataset.<br>Use the `ExcelOptions` property to define how DataBrew will interpret a Microsoft Excel file when<br>creating a dataset from that file.<br>Use the `FilesLimit` property to limit the number of<br>Amazon S3 files that should be selected for a dataset<br>from a connected Amazon S3 path.<br>Use the `FilterExpression` property to define parameter<br>conditions.<br>Use the `FilterValue` property to define a single entry<br>in the `ValuesMap` of a<br>`FilterExpression`.<br>Use the `FormatOptions` property to define the<br>structure of either comma-separated value (CSV), Excel, or JSON<br>input.<br>Use the `Input` property to define how DataBrew can find data, in either the AWS Glue Data Catalog or Amazon S3.<br>Use the `JsonOptions` property to define how input is<br>to be interpreted by AWS Glue DataBrew.<br>Use the `PathOptions` property to define how DataBrew selects files for a given Amazon S3<br>path in a dataset.<br>Use the `PathParameter` property to define the file<br>format of a dataset.<br>Use the `S3Location` property to define a single entry<br>in the path parameters of a dataset.<br>[AWS::DataBrew::Job](../UserGuide/aws-resource-databrew-job.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-databrew-job.md")<br>Use the `JobSample` property to define the number of<br>rows on which a profile job is run.<br>Use the `OutputLocation` property to define the<br>location in Amazon S3 where the job writes its output.<br>Use the `Recipe` property to define the actions to be<br>performed on a dataset. Support for AMI ID formats lets you avoid updating<br>all your scripts and templates with a new ID each time the AMI that<br>you want to use in your processes changes. You can create a<br>parameter with the data type `aws:ec2:image`, and for its<br>value, enter the ID of an AMI. This is the AMI from which you<br>currently want new instances to be created. You then reference this<br>parameter in your templates and commands. When you’re ready to use a<br>different AMI, update the parameter value. Parameter Store validates<br>the new AMI ID, and you don’t need to update your scripts and<br>templates. This is used to specify and configure a log<br>router for container logs.<br>In the [LinuxParameters](../UserGuide/aws-properties-ecs-taskdefinition-linuxparameters.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-ecs-taskdefinition-linuxparameters.md") property type:<br>• use the `MaxSwap` property to specify the total amount<br>of swap memory (in MiB) a container can use.<br>• use the `Swappiness` property to tune a container's<br>memory swappiness behavior. | Updated resources                                                                                                                                                                                                  | The following resources were updated:<br>`AWS::ApplicationAutoScaling::ScalableTarget`,<br>`AWS::DynamoDB::Table`, `AWS::EC2::Instance`,<br>`AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition`,<br>`AWS::ElastiCache::ReplicationGroup`, `AWS::Events::Rule`,<br>`AWS::IAM::Role`, and<br>`AWS::Lambda::EventSourceMapping`.<br>[AWS::ApplicationAutoScaling::ScalableTarget](aws-resource-applicationautoscaling-scalabletarget.md "aws-resource-applicationautoscaling-scalabletarget.md")<br>Use the `SuspendedState` property to suspend and resume<br>automatic scaling. Setting the value of an attribute to `true`<br>suspends the specified scaling activities. Setting it to<br>`false` (default) resumes the specified scaling<br>activities.<br>[AWS::DynamoDB::Table](aws-resource-dynamodb-table.md "aws-resource-dynamodb-table.md")<br>In the [SSESpecification](aws-properties-dynamodb-table-ssespecification.md "aws-properties-dynamodb-table-ssespecification.md") property type, use the `SSEType`<br>property to specify server-side encryption type.<br>[AWS::EC2::Instance](aws-resource-ec2-instance.md "aws-resource-ec2-instance.md")<br>Use the `CpuOptions` property to specify the CPU options<br>for the instance.<br>In the [Ebs](aws-properties-ec2-instance-ebs.md "aws-properties-ec2-instance-ebs.md")<br>property type, use the `KmsKeyId` property to specify an<br>identifier (key ID, key alias, ID ARN, or alias ARN) for a customer managed key<br>under which the EBS volume is encrypted.<br>[AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition](aws-resource-ecs-taskdefinition.md "aws-resource-ecs-taskdefinition.md")<br>Use the `IpcMode` property to specify the IPC resource<br>namespace to use for the containers in the task. The valid values are<br>`host`, `task`, or `none`.<br>Use the `PidMode` property to specify the process namespace<br>to use for the containers in the task. The valid values are<br>`host` or `task`.<br>In the [ContainerDefinition](aws-properties-ecs-taskdefinition-containerdefinitions.md "aws-properties-ecs-taskdefinition-containerdefinitions.md") property type:<br>• When the `Interactive` property is set to<br>`true`, this allows you to deploy containerized<br>applications that require `stdin` or a `tty`<br>to be allocated.<br>• When the `PseudoTerminal` proprety is set to<br>`true`, a TTY is allocated.<br>• Use the `SystemControls` property to specify a list<br>of namespaced kernel parameters to set in the container.<br>In the [LogConfiguration](aws-properties-ecs-taskdefinition-containerdefinitions-logconfiguration.md "aws-properties-ecs-taskdefinition-containerdefinitions-logconfiguration.md") property type, use the<br>`SecretOptions` property to specify the secrets to pass to<br>the log configuration.<br>[AWS::ElastiCache::ReplicationGroup](aws-resource-elasticache-replicationgroup.md "aws-resource-elasticache-replicationgroup.md")<br>Use the `KmsKeyId` property to specify the ID of the<br>KMS key used to encrypt the disk on the cluster.<br>[AWS::Events::Rule](aws-resource-events-rule.md "aws-resource-events-rule.md")<br>In the [EcsParameters](aws-properties-events-rule-ecsparameters.md "aws-properties-events-rule-ecsparameters.md") property type:<br>• Use the `Group` property to specify an ECS task group<br>for the task.<br>• Use the `LaunchType` property to specify the launch<br>type on which your task is running.<br>• If the ECS task uses the `awsvpc` network mode, use<br>the `NetworkConfiguration` property to specify the VPC<br>subnets and security groups associated with the task and whether a<br>public IP address is to be used.<br>• Use the `PlatformVersion` property to specify the<br>platform version for the task.<br>[AWS::IAM::Role](aws-resource-iam-role.md "aws-resource-iam-role.md")<br>Use the `Description` property to provide a description for<br>the role.<br>Use the `Tags` property to specify a list of tags that are<br>attached to the specified role.<br>[AWS::Lambda::EventSourceMapping](aws-resource-lambda-eventsourcemapping.md "aws-resource-lambda-eventsourcemapping.md")<br>Use the `MaximumBatchingWindowInSeconds` property to<br>specify the maximum amount of time to gather records before invoking the<br>function, in seconds. | Updated resources                                                                                                                                                                                                  | The following resources were updated: `AWS::Batch::JobDefinition`,<br>`AWS::Cognito::UserPool`, `AWS::Cognito::UserPoolClient`,<br>and `AWS::Glue::Job`.<br>[AWS::Batch::JobDefinition](aws-resource-batch-jobdefinition.md "aws-resource-batch-jobdefinition.md")<br>In the [ContainerProperties](aws-properties-batch-jobdefinition-containerproperties.md "aws-properties-batch-jobdefinition-containerproperties.md") property type, use the<br>`LinuxParameters` property to specify Linux-specific<br>modifications that are applied to the container, such as details for<br>device mappings.<br>[AWS::Cognito::UserPool](aws-resource-cognito-userpool.md "aws-resource-cognito-userpool.md")<br>Use the `UserPoolAddOns` property to enable advanced<br>security risk detection.<br>Use the `VerificationMessageTemplate` property to define<br>the template for verification messages.<br>[AWS::Cognito::UserPoolClient](aws-resource-cognito-userpoolclient.md "aws-resource-cognito-userpoolclient.md")<br>Use the `AnalyticsConfiguration` property to define the<br>Amazon Pinpoint analytics configuration for collecting metrics for this user<br>pool.<br>[AWS::Glue::Job](aws-resource-glue-job.md "aws-resource-glue-job.md")<br>Use the `GlueVersion` property to determine the versions of<br>Apache Spark and Python that AWS Glue supports. The Python version indicates<br>the version supported for jobs of type Spark.<br>Use the `MaxCapacity` property to specify the number of<br>AWS Glue data processing units (DPUs) that can be allocated when this<br>job runs. A DPU is a relative measure of processing power that consists<br>of 4 vCPUs of compute capacity and 16 GB of memory.<br>For the `NumberofWorkers` property, when you specify a<br>Python shell job (`JobCommand.Name`="pythonshell"), you can<br>allocate either 0.0625 or 1 DPU. The default is 0.0625 DPU. When you<br>specify an Apache Spark ETL job (`JobCommand.Name`="glueetl"),<br>you can allocate from 2 to 100 DPUs. The default is 10 DPUs. This job<br>type can't have a fractional DPU allocation.<br>Use the `WorkerType` property to specify the type of<br>predefined worker that is allocated when a job runs.<br>In the [JobCommand](aws-properties-glue-job-jobcommand.md "aws-properties-glue-job-jobcommand.md") property type, use the `PythonVersion`<br>property to specify the Python version being used to execute a Python<br>shell job. | New resources                                                                                                                                                                                                      | The following resources were added: `AWS::MediaLive::Channel`,<br>`AWS::MediaLive::Input`, and<br>`AWS::MediaLive::InputSecurityGroup`.<br>[AWS::MediaLive::Channel](aws-resource-medialive-channel.md "aws-resource-medialive-channel.md")<br>The `AWS::MediaLive::Channel` resource creates a channel. A<br>MediaLive channel ingests and transcodes (decodes and encodes) source<br>content from the inputs that are attached to that channel, and packages<br>the new content into outputs.<br>[AWS::MediaLive::Input](aws-resource-medialive-input.md "aws-resource-medialive-input.md")<br>The `AWS::MediaLive::Input` resource creates an input. A<br>MediaLive input holds information that describes how the MediaLive<br>channel is connected to the upstream system that is providing the source<br>content that is to be transcoded.<br>[AWS::MediaLive::InputSecurityGroup](aws-resource-medialive-inputsecuritygroup.md "aws-resource-medialive-inputsecuritygroup.md")<br>The `AWS::MediaLive::InputSecurityGroup` resource creates<br>an input security group. A MediaLive input security group is associated<br>with a MediaLive input. The input security group is an "allow list" of IP<br>addresses that controls whether an external IP address can push content<br>to the associated MediaLive input. To disable backtracking, specify 0.
